title.en: Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21 - Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang
title.raw: 卷六十九 唐書45: 列傳21 張憲 王正言 胡裝 崔貽孫 孟鵠 孫岳 張延朗 劉延皓 劉延朗 Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21 - Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang

sentences.zh: 張憲，字允中，晉陽人，世以軍功為牙校。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian, courtesy name Yunzhong, was a man of Jinyang. For generations his family had held the post of yaxiao through military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, courtesy name Yunzhong, was a native of Jinyang. For generations his family had earned the rank of yaxiao through military service.

sentences.zh: 憲始童丱，喜儒學，勵志橫經，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: From the time Xian was a child in topknot, he delighted in Confucian learning, resolved to traverse the classics horizontally, and did not cease day or night.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xian loved Confucian learning, set his heart on mastering the classics, and studied without rest day or night.

sentences.zh: 太原地雄邊服，人多尚武，恥於學業，惟憲與里人藥縱之精力遊學，弱冠盡通諸經，尤精《左傳》。

translations.literal: Taiyuan's territory was strong on the frontier; most people valued martial affairs and were ashamed of scholarly pursuit. Only Xian and a fellow townsman, Yao Zong, with vigorous energy traveled to study abroad; at weak-capping age he had thoroughly mastered all the classics, and was especially expert in the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was a powerful frontier region where most people prized martial prowess and looked down on scholarship. Only Xian and a townsman named Yao Zong threw themselves into study away from home; by his coming of age Xian had mastered all the classics and was especially versed in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 嘗袖行所業，謁判官李襲吉，一見欣歎。

translations.literal: Once he carried in his sleeve the writings he had produced and called on the judicial intendant Li Xiji; at one sight he exclaimed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Once he tucked his writings into his sleeve and called on the judicial intendant Li Xiji, who exclaimed in admiration at first sight.

sentences.zh: 既辭，謂憲曰：「子勉之，將來必成佳器。

translations.literal: When he had taken his leave, he said to Xian, "You exert yourself; in the future you will surely become a fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: As Xian was leaving, Li said to him, "Apply yourself—you are sure to become a man of real accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 」石州刺史楊守業喜聚書，以家書示之，聞見日博。

translations.literal: " The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, delighted in collecting books and showed him his family library; his knowledge and experience grew daily broader.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Shouye, prefect of Shizhou, was a collector of books and showed Xian his family library, so that his learning broadened day by day.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為行軍司馬，廣延髦俊，素知憲名，令朱守殷齎書幣延之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was campaigning marshal, he widely extended invitations to eminent talents; having long known Xian's name, he ordered Zhu Shouyin to carry letters and gifts to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong served as campaigning marshal, he sought out eminent men far and wide. Knowing Xian's reputation, he sent Zhu Shouyin with letters and gifts to invite him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，釋褐交城令，秩滿，莊宗嗣世，補太原府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left the commoner's cloth and became magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term was complete and Zhuangzong succeeded to the succession, he was appointed recorder of the Taiyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he entered office as magistrate of Jiaocheng. When his term ended and Zhuangzong succeeded to power, he was appointed recorder of the Taiyuan prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 時霸府初開，幕客馬鬱、王緘，燕中名士，盡與之遊。

translations.literal: At that time the hegemon's headquarters had just been opened; staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, famous scholars of Yan, all associated with him in travel.
translations.idiomatic: The hegemon's headquarters had just been established, and he associated with staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, celebrated scholars from the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 十二年，莊宗平河朔，念藩邸之舊，征赴行台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei, mindful of old ties from the princely residence, and summoned him to the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after Zhuangzong pacified Hebei, he recalled Xian to the field headquarters out of regard for their old ties at the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授監察，賜緋，署魏博推官，自是恒簪筆扈從。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed investigating censor, granted scarlet robes, and assigned as pushi of Weibo; from then on he constantly wore the writing brush and attended in escort.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made investigating censor, granted scarlet robes, and appointed pushi of Weibo; from then on he always carried his writing brush in the emperor's retinue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，王師戰胡柳，周德威軍不利，憲與同列奔馬北渡；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the royal army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army met with ill fortune, and Xian with his colleagues galloped north across the river;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu. When Zhou Dewei's forces fared badly, Xian and his colleagues galloped north to cross the river;

sentences.zh: 梁軍急追，殆將不濟。

translations.literal: the Liang army pressed in pursuit, and they were nearly unable to get across.
translations.idiomatic: the Liang army pressed hard in pursuit, and they nearly failed to escape.

sentences.zh: 至晚渡河，人皆陷水而沒，憲與從子朗履冰而行；

translations.literal: By evening they crossed the river; people all sank in the water and perished. Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice;
translations.idiomatic: By evening they crossed the river. Many men sank and drowned in the water, but Xian and his nephew Lang walked across on the ice;

sentences.zh: 將及岸，冰陷，朗泣，以馬箠引之，憲曰：「吾兒去矣，勿使俱陷。

translations.literal: when they were about to reach the bank the ice gave way. Lang wept and pulled him with a riding crop. Xian said, "My boy, go—do not let us both sink.
translations.idiomatic: and as they neared the bank the ice broke. Lang wept and pulled him with a riding crop. Xian said, "My boy, go on—do not let us both go under.

sentences.zh: 」朗曰：「忍季父如此，俱死無恨。

translations.literal: " Lang said, "To bear my uncle's junior thus—to die together would be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: " Lang said, "How can I leave my uncle to this? To die together would be no regret.

sentences.zh: 」朗偃伏引箠，憲躍身而出。

translations.literal: " Lang lay prostrate and pulled with the crop; Xian leaped and came out.
translations.idiomatic: " Lang lay flat and pulled with the crop while Xian sprang free.

sentences.zh: 是夜，莊宗令於軍中求憲，或曰：「與王緘俱歿矣！

translations.literal: That night Zhuangzong ordered that Xian be sought in the army. Someone said, "He has perished together with Wang Jian!
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhuangzong ordered the army to search for Xian. Someone said, "He has perished together with Wang Jian!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗垂涕求屍，數日，聞其免也，遣使慰勞。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong shed tears and sought his corpse. After several days he heard that he had escaped, and sent an envoy to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong wept and ordered a search for his body. Several days later, hearing that Xian had survived, he sent an envoy to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 尋改掌書記、水部郎中，賜金紫，曆魏博觀察判官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was changed to chief secretary and director of the Water Ministry, granted gold and purple, and successively served as administrative aide of the Weibo observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made chief secretary and director of the Water Ministry, granted gold and purple insignia, and served successively as administrative aide of the Weibo observation commission.

sentences.zh: 從討張文禮，鎮州平，授魏、博、鎮、冀十郡觀察判官，改考功郎中，兼御史中丞，權鎮州留事。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Zhang Wenli; when Zhenzhou was pacified he was appointed administrative aide of the observation commission over ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, changed to director of the Ministry of Personnel Evaluation, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, and acting charge of Zhenzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign against Zhang Wenli. When Zhenzhou was pacified he was made administrative aide for the ten-prefecture observation commission of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director of the Ministry of Personnel Evaluation and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with acting charge of Zhenzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，詔還魏都，授尚書工部侍郎，充租庸使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, an edict recalled him to the Wei capital; he was appointed vice minister of the Works in the Secretariat and made commissioner of the grain and corvée tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was recalled to the Wei capital by edict, appointed vice minister of works in the Secretariat, and made commissioner of the grain and corvée tax.

sentences.zh: 八月，改刑部侍郎，判吏部銓，兼太清宮副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was changed to vice minister of punishments, judged the Ministry of Personnel selection, and concurrently served as deputy commissioner of the Great Pure Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made vice minister of punishments, placed in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently appointed deputy commissioner of the Great Pure Palace.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遷洛陽，以憲檢校吏部尚書、興唐尹、東京副留守，知留守事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong moved to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, Xingtang prefect, and deputy eastern capital intendant, with charge of the intendant's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong moved the capital to Luoyang, Xian was appointed acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, and deputy eastern capital intendant in charge of the capital's affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲學識優深，尤精吏道，剖析聽斷，人不敢欺。

translations.literal: Xian's learning and knowledge were excellent and profound; he was especially expert in the way of officials. In analysis and hearing of cases no one dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's learning was deep and his grasp of administration especially keen; in hearing cases and weighing evidence, no one dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 三年春，車駕幸鄴，時易定王都來朝，宴於行宮，將擊鞠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the imperial carriage visited Ye. At that time the Prince of Yiding, Wang Du, came to court; they feasted at the traveling palace and were about to play cuju.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor visited Ye. The Prince of Yiding, Wang Du, had come to court, and at the traveling palace a feast was held before a planned game of cuju.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗行即位之禮，卜鞠場吉，因築壇於其間，至是詔毀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong performed the rites of accession, divination on the cuju ground was auspicious, and therefore an altar was built in its midst. At this time an edict ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhuangzong performed his accession rites, divination on the cuju ground had been auspicious, and an altar had been built there. Now an edict ordered it torn down.

sentences.zh: 憲奏曰：「即位壇是陛下祭接天神受命之所，自風燥雨濡之外，不可輒毀，亦不可修。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized, saying, "The accession altar is the place where Your Majesty sacrificed to receive Heaven's mandate from the spirits. Apart from when wind has dried it or rain has soaked it, it must not be rashly destroyed, nor may it be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Xian memorialized: "The accession altar is where Your Majesty received Heaven's mandate through sacrifice. Apart from damage by wind or rain, it must not be destroyed on a whim, nor should it be repaired casually.

sentences.zh: 魏繁陽之壇，漢汜水之墠，到今猶有兆象。

translations.literal: The altar at Fanyang in Wei and the mound at Sishui in Han—even to the present there remain traces and signs.
translations.idiomatic: The altar at Fanyang in Wei and the mound at Sishui under the Han—even now their traces remain.

sentences.zh: 存而不毀，古之道也。

translations.literal: To preserve and not destroy is the way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve and not destroy them is the way of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」即命治之於宮西。

translations.literal: " He was immediately ordered to repair it west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately ordered to restore it west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 數日，未成。

translations.literal: After several days it was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Several days passed, and the work was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 會憲以公事獲謫，閣門待罪，上怒，戒有司速治行宮之庭，礙事者畢去，竟毀即位壇。

translations.literal: It happened that Xian was demoted on account of official business and awaited punishment at the palace gate. The sovereign was angry and warned the officials to quickly prepare the traveling palace courtyard; whatever obstructed the affair was entirely removed, and in the end the accession altar was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was then demoted on official charges and awaited punishment at the palace gate. The emperor was angry and ordered officials to prepare the traveling palace courtyard at once; everything in the way was cleared away, and the accession altar was destroyed after all.

sentences.zh: 憲私謂郭崇韜曰：「不祥之甚，忽其本也。」

translations.literal: Xian privately said to Guo Chongtao, "This is most inauspicious—neglecting the root."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said privately to Guo Chongtao, "This is a grave ill omen—they have forgotten the foundation."

sentences.zh: 秋，崇韜將兵征蜀，以手書告憲曰：「允中避事久矣，餘受命西征，已奏還公黃閣。

translations.literal: In autumn Chongtao was about to lead troops on the western campaign against Shu and wrote Xian in his own hand, saying, "Yunzhong has long avoided affairs. I have received orders for the western expedition and have already memorialized to return you to the Yellow Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, as Chongtao was preparing to lead troops against Shu, he wrote Xian in his own hand: "Yunzhong, you have long kept out of court affairs. I have received orders for the western campaign and have already memorialized to bring you back to the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 」憲報曰：「庖人之代屍祝，所謂非吾事也。

translations.literal: " Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the invocator of the corpse—this is what is called not my affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the priest at sacrifice—that is what people call 'not my business.'

sentences.zh: 」時樞密承旨段徊當權任事，以憲從龍舊望，不欲憲在朝廷。

translations.literal: " At that time Duan Huai, bearer of edicts at the Bureau of Military Affairs, held power and managed affairs; because of Xian's old prestige as a follower of the dragon, he did not want Xian in the court.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Duan Huai of the Bureau of Military Affairs held power and managed affairs. Because of Xian's long-standing prestige as a companion of Zhuangzong's rise, he did not want Xian at court.

sentences.zh: 會孟知祥鎮蜀川，選北京留守，徊揚言曰：「北門，國家根本，非重德不可輕授；

translations.literal: It happened that Meng Zhixiang was stationed in Shu and the northern capital intendant was to be chosen. Huai proclaimed publicly, "The northern gate is the root of the state; without weighty virtue it cannot be lightly conferred;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang was posted to Shu and a northern capital intendant was to be chosen, Huai declared publicly, "The northern gate is the foundation of the state. Without great virtue it must not be lightly entrusted;

sentences.zh: 今之取才，非憲不可。

translations.literal: in selecting talent for this post, none but Xian will do.
translations.idiomatic: for this appointment no one but Xian will do.

sentences.zh: 」趨時者因附徊勢，巧中傷之。

translations.literal: " Those who courted the times therefore attached themselves to Huai's power and craftily slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who courted favor attached themselves to Huai's power and craftily slandered Xian.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「憲有相業，然國祚中興，宰相在天子麵前，得失可以改作；

translations.literal: He also said, "Xian has the capacity of a chief minister, yet with the restoration of the dynastic fortune, a chief minister stands before the Son of Heaven and gains and losses can be revised;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xian has the makings of a chief minister, but with the restoration of the dynasty a chief minister stands before the Son of Heaven and his errors can be corrected;

sentences.zh: 一方之事，製在一人，惟北面事重。

translations.literal: affairs of one region are controlled by a single man, and only matters of the northern quarter are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: affairs of a single region rest in one man's hands, and only the northern quarter is weighty.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，授憲銀青光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、太原尹、北京留守，知府事。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month Xian was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, acting minister of personnel, prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital intendant, and in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month Xian was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, acting minister of personnel, prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital intendant, and administrator of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮入魏州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時憲家屬在魏，關東俶擾，在禮善待其家，遣人齎書至太原誘憲。

translations.literal: At that time Xian's family were in Wei; east of the pass there was sudden turmoil. Zaili treated his family well and sent a man bearing a letter to Taiyuan to entice Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's family were then in Wei. With turmoil erupting east of the pass, Zaili treated them well and sent a man with a letter to Taiyuan to win Xian over.

sentences.zh: 憲斬其使，書不發函而奏。

translations.literal: Xian beheaded the envoy, did not open the letter's cover, and memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian beheaded the envoy, sent the letter to court unopened, and memorialized about the incident.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗為兵眾所劫，諸軍離散，地遠不知事實，或謂憲曰：「蜀軍未至，洛陽窘急，總管又失兵權，製在諸軍之手，又聞河朔推戴，事若實然，或可濟否？

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Mingzong was coerced by the troops; the armies scattered. The distance was great and the facts were unknown. Someone said to Xian, "The Shu army has not yet arrived; Luoyang is in dire straits; the commander-in-chief has also lost military authority, and control is in the hands of the armies. Moreover it is heard that Hebei is pushing for enthronement—if the matter is truly so, might it perhaps succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Mingzong was seized by the troops and the armies scattered. Far away in Taiyuan, the facts were unclear. Someone said to Xian, "The Shu army has not arrived; Luoyang is desperate; the commander-in-chief has lost control of the troops, and power rests with the armies. We also hear that Hebei is pressing for enthronement—if that is true, might we succeed?

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「治亂之機，間不容發，以愚所斷，事未可知。

translations.literal: " Xian said, "The pivot of order and chaos admits no interval. By my dull judgment, the outcome cannot yet be known.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "The turning point between order and chaos allows no delay. By my poor judgment, the outcome is still unknown.

sentences.zh: 愚聞藥縱之言，總管德量仁厚，素得士心，餘勿多言，誌此而已。

translations.literal: I have heard Yao Zong's words: the commander-in-chief's virtue and measure are benevolent and generous, and he has long won the hearts of the officers. Say no more—record only this.
translations.idiomatic: I recall what Yao Zong once said: the commander-in-chief is benevolent and magnanimous and has long won the hearts of his men. Say no more—remember only this.

sentences.zh: 」四月五日，李存渥自洛陽至，口傳莊宗命，並無書詔，惟云天子授以隻箭，傳之為信。

translations.literal: " On the fifth day of the fourth month Li Cunwo came from Luoyang, orally transmitting Zhuangzong's command. There was no written edict—only that the Son of Heaven had given a single arrow, and passing it on was the proof.
translations.idiomatic: " On the fifth day of the fourth month Li Cunwo arrived from Luoyang with Zhuangzong's orders by word of mouth. There was no written edict—only the claim that the Son of Heaven had given a single arrow as token of authority.

sentences.zh: 眾心惑之，時事莫測。

translations.literal: The hearts of the crowd were perplexed; the times could not be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: The men were perplexed and the situation impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 左右獻畫曰：「存渥所乘馬，已戢其飾，復召人謀事，必行陰禍，因欲據城。

translations.literal: Those at his side offered a plan, saying, "The horse Cunwo rides has already had its trappings removed. He has again summoned men to plot affairs—he will surely carry out a hidden treachery and therefore wishes to seize the city.
translations.idiomatic: His advisers offered a plan: "The horse Cunwo rides has already had its trappings removed. He has summoned men again to plot—he surely intends treachery and means to seize the city.

sentences.zh: 寧我負人，宜早為之所，但戮呂、鄭二宦，且係存渥，徐觀其變，事萬全矣。

translations.literal: Better that I wrong others—one should act early. Only kill the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, and for the time being detain Cunwo; watch the changes slowly, and the affair will be wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: Better to wrong others than be wronged—act at once. Kill only the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, detain Cunwo for the moment, watch how events unfold, and all will be secure.

sentences.zh: 」憲良久曰：「吾本書生，無軍功而致身及此，一旦自布衣而紆金紫，向來仕宦非出他門，此畫非吾心也。

translations.literal: " Xian was silent a long while and said, "I am originally a scholar; without military achievement I have reached this position. In a single day I went from common cloth to purple and gold. My official career has not come from another gate—this plan is not my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was silent a long while, then said, "I am a scholar by origin. Without military merit I have risen to this rank, and in a day I went from common cloth to gold and purple. My whole career has come through one patron alone—this plan is not in my heart.

sentences.zh: 事苟不濟，以身徇義。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, I will offer my body in devotion to righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, I will give my life for righteousness."

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·張昭傳》：昭勸憲奉表明宗以勸進，憲曰：「吾書生也，天子委以保厘之任，吾豈苟生者乎！

translations.literal: (Biography of Zhang Zhao in the Brief Account of the Eastern Capital: Zhao urged Xian to submit a memorial to Mingzong to urge his advance to the throne. Xian said, "I am a scholar. The Son of Heaven entrusted me with the duty of guarding and soothing—how could I be one who clings to life!
translations.idiomatic: (Brief Account of the Eastern Capital, Biography of Zhang Zhao: Zhao urged Xian to submit a memorial urging Mingzong to take the throne. Xian said, "I am a scholar. The Son of Heaven entrusted me with guarding the realm—how could I cling to life!

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「此古之大節，公能行之，忠臣也。

translations.literal: " Zhao said, "This is the great integrity of antiquity. If the lord can carry it out, he is a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao said, "That is the great integrity of antiquity. If you can do this, you are a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」憲既死，論者以昭能成憲之節。）〉

translations.literal: " After Xian died, commentators held that Zhao was able to complete Xian's integrity.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " After Xian's death, commentators held that Zhao had helped Xian fulfill his integrity.)〉

sentences.zh: 翌日，符彥超誅呂、鄭，軍城大亂，燔剽達曙。

translations.literal: The next day Fu Yanchao killed Lü and Zheng; the army city fell into great disorder, and burning and plunder continued until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fu Yanchao killed Lü and Zheng. The garrison city fell into chaos, and looting and fires continued until dawn.

sentences.zh: 憲初聞有變，出奔沂州。

translations.literal: When Xian first heard of the disturbance he fled to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian first heard of the upheaval he fled to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而有司糾其委城之罪，四月二十四日，賜死於晉陽之千佛院。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the authorities impeached him for the crime of abandoning the city. On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month he was granted death at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the authorities charged him with abandoning the city. On the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month he was ordered to take his own life at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 幼子凝隨父走，亦為收者加害。

translations.literal: His young son Ning followed his father in flight and was also harmed by those who seized them.
translations.idiomatic: His young son Ning fled with him and was also killed by those who captured them.

sentences.zh: 明宗郊禮大赦，有司請昭雪，從之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong performed the suburban rite and proclaimed a great amnesty, the authorities requested that his name be cleared, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty, the authorities petitioned to clear Xian's name, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 憲沈靜寡欲，喜聚圖書，家書五千卷，視事之餘，手自刊校。

translations.literal: Xian was deep, tranquil, and of few desires; he delighted in collecting books. His family library had five thousand scrolls, and in the intervals of conducting affairs he personally collated and corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was reserved and abstemious, fond of collecting books. His family library held five thousand scrolls, and in the intervals of official business he personally collated them.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，不飲酒，賓僚宴語，但論文嘯詠而已，士友重之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither and did not drink wine. At banquets with guests and staff he spoke only of literature and chanting poetry; scholars and friends esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither well and did not drink. At gatherings with guests and colleagues he spoke only of literature and poetry, and men of learning held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 憲長子守素，仕晉，位至尚書。

translations.literal: Xian's eldest son Shousu served Jin and reached the post of minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's eldest son Shousu served the Jin court and rose to minister.

sentences.zh: 王正言，鄆州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan was a native of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父誌，濟陰令。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was magistrate of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was magistrate of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 正言早孤貧，從沙門學，工詩，密州刺史賀德倫令歸俗，署郡職。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was early orphaned and poor; he studied with Buddhist monks and was skilled at poetry. He Delun, prefect of Mizhou, ordered him to return to the laity and appointed him to a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan was orphaned young and poor. He studied under Buddhist monks and excelled at poetry. He Delun, prefect of Mizhou, ordered him to return to lay life and gave him a post in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德倫鎮青州，表為推官；

translations.literal: When Delun was stationed at Qingzhou he recommended him as pushi;
translations.idiomatic: When Delun was posted to Qingzhou he recommended Zhengyan as pushi;

sentences.zh: 移鎮魏州，改觀察判官。

translations.literal: when he moved his command to Weizhou, he was changed to administrative aide of the observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: and when Delun moved his command to Weizhou, Zhengyan became administrative aide of the observation commission.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定魏博，正言仍舊職任，小心端慎，與物無競。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan remained in his former office. He was careful, upright, and cautious, and did not compete with others.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan kept his post. He was careful, upright, and uncontentious.

sentences.zh: 嘗為同職司空頲所淩，正言降心下之。

translations.literal: Once he was bullied by his colleague of the same office, Sikong Hui; Zhengyan lowered his heart and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was once bullied by a colleague of equal rank, Sikong Hui, but Zhengyan humbled himself and yielded.

sentences.zh: 頲誅，代為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Hui was executed, he replaced him as military commissioner aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was executed, Zhengyan replaced him as military commissioner aide.

sentences.zh: 同光初，守戶部尚書、興唐尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he held the posts of minister of revenue and Xingtang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tongguang era he served as minister of revenue and prefect of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙為租庸副使，常畏張憲挺特，不欲其領使，乃白郭崇韜留憲於魏州，請宰相豆盧革判租庸。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian was deputy commissioner of the grain and corvée tax and often feared Zhang Xian's uprightness; he did not want him to head the commission and therefore told Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Weizhou, requesting that the chief minister Doulu Ge judge the grain and corvée tax.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian was then deputy commissioner of the grain and corvée tax. He feared Zhang Xian's uncompromising character and did not want him to head the office, so he persuaded Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Weizhou and asked that chief minister Doulu Ge oversee the grain and corvée tax.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以盧質代之。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Zhi was again substituted in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu Zhi replaced Doulu Ge in the role.

sentences.zh: 孔謙白云：「錢穀重務，宰相事多，簿籍留滯。

translations.literal: Kong Qian reported to the sovereign, saying, "Revenue is a weighty affair; the chief minister has many duties, and the ledgers are delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian told the emperor, "Revenue is a weighty matter, but the chief minister has too many duties and the accounts pile up.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「盧質判二日，便借官錢，皆不可任。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Lu Zhi, after judging for two days, immediately borrowed official funds—none of them can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Lu Zhi borrowed official funds after only two days in charge—none of them is fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 」意謂崇韜必令己代其任，時物議未允而止，謙沮喪久之。

translations.literal: " He meant that Chongtao would surely have him replace that duty. At the time public opinion did not consent and it stopped; Qian was dejected for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " He expected Chongtao to appoint him in their place, but public opinion would not allow it and the plan failed. Qian was dejected for a long time.

sentences.zh: 李紹宏曰：「邦計國本，時號怨府，非張憲不稱職。

translations.literal: Li Shaohong said, "State revenue is the root of the nation; it is at the time called the office of complaints. None but Zhang Xian is fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong said, "State revenue is the foundation of the realm—it is called the office of popular complaint. No one but Zhang Xian is fit for it.

sentences.zh: 」即日征之。

translations.literal: " That very day he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: " That very day Xian was summoned.

sentences.zh: 孔謙、段徊白崇韜曰：「邦計雖重，在侍中眼前，但得一人為使即可。

translations.literal: Kong Qian and Duan Huai told Chongtao, saying, "Although state revenue is weighty, it is before the Vice Director's eyes; it is enough to have one man as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian and Duan Huai told Chongtao, "Revenue is important, but it is under the Vice Director's eye—any competent man will do as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 魏博六州戶口，天下之半，王正言操守有餘，智力不足，若朝廷任使，庶幾與人共事；

translations.literal: The six prefectures of Weibo account for half the population under Heaven. Wang Zhengyan has integrity in surplus but intelligence and strength insufficient. If the court employs him, he might perhaps work with others;
translations.idiomatic: The six prefectures of Weibo hold half the empire's population. Wang Zhengyan has integrity to spare but lacks ability. In a court appointment he might work under others;

sentences.zh: 若專製方隅，未見其可。

translations.literal: if he were to monopolize control of a region, one does not yet see that this would do.
translations.idiomatic: but to give him sole control of a region would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 張憲才器兼濟，宜以委之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian's talent and capacity are both fulfilled—he should be entrusted with it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian has both talent and capacity and should be entrusted with the post.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜即奏憲留守魏州，征王正言為租庸使。

translations.literal: " Chongtao immediately memorialized that Xian remain intendant at Weizhou and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner of the grain and corvée tax.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongtao at once memorialized to keep Xian as intendant at Weizhou and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner of the grain and corvée tax.

sentences.zh: 正言在職，主諾而已，權柄出於孔謙。

translations.literal: In office Zhengyan merely assented; real authority lay with Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In office Zhengyan merely assented to decisions; real power lay with Kong Qian.

sentences.zh: 正言不耐繁浩，簿領縱橫，觸事遺忘，物論以為不可，即以孔謙代之，正言守禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhengyan could not bear the complexity and volume; documents and ledgers lay crisscross, and in every matter he forgot. Public opinion held that this would not do, and Kong Qian was immediately substituted in his place; Zhengyan remained minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan could not cope with the complexity. Documents piled up and he forgot matters at every turn. Public opinion judged him unfit, and Kong Qian replaced him while Zhengyan remained minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，代張憲為興唐尹，留守鄴都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as Xingtang prefect and remained intendant at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as prefect of Xingtang and remained intendant at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 時武德使史彥瓊，監守鄴都，廩帑出納，兵馬製置，皆出彥瓊，將佐官吏，頤指氣使，正言不能以道禦之，但趑趄聽命。

translations.literal: At that time the martial virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong supervised and guarded Yedu; disbursement of granaries and treasuries and disposition of troops and horses all issued from Yanqiong. Generals, aides, and officials he commanded with chin and breath; Zhengyan could not control him by the Way but only hesitated and obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The martial virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong then supervised Yedu. Granaries, treasuries, troops, and horses were all under his control, and officers and officials obeyed his every gesture. Zhengyan could not restrain him by proper authority and only shrank back and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至是，貝州戍兵亂，入魏州，彥瓊望風敗走，亂兵剽劫坊市。

translations.literal: At this time the garrison troops of Beizhou mutinied and entered Weizhou. Yanqiong fled at the sight of the wind; the mutinous troops plundered the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Beizhou garrison mutinied and entered Weizhou. Yanqiong fled at the first alarm while the mutineers looted the wards and markets.

sentences.zh: 正言促召書吏寫奏章，家人曰：「賊已殺人縱火，都城已陷，何奏之有。

translations.literal: Zhengyan urgently summoned clerks to write a memorial. His family said, "The bandits have already killed people and set fires; the capital has fallen—what memorial is there to write?
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan urgently summoned clerks to draft a memorial. His family said, "The rebels are already killing and burning—the capital has fallen. What is there to memorialize?

sentences.zh: 」是日，正言引諸僚佐謁趙在禮，

translations.literal: " That day Zhengyan led all his staff to call on Zhao Zaili,
translations.idiomatic: " That day Zhengyan led his staff to call on Zhao Zaili,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：正言索馬，不能得，乃帥僚佐步出府門謁在禮。）〉

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Zhengyan sought a horse but could not obtain one, and therefore led his staff on foot out the prefectural gate to call on Zaili.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhengyan sought a horse but could not get one, so he led his staff on foot out the prefectural gate to call on Zaili.)〉

sentences.zh: 望塵再拜請罪。

translations.literal: bowing twice in the dust to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: bowing repeatedly in the dust to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 在禮曰：「尚書重德，勿自卑屈，餘受國恩，與尚書共事，但思歸之眾，倉卒見迫耳。

translations.literal: Zaili said, "The Minister's virtue is weighty—do not humble yourself. I have received the state's grace and serve together with the Minister; it is only that the crowd longing to return home was hastily pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili said, "Minister, your virtue is great—do not demean yourself. I have received the state's grace and serve alongside you. It is only that the men, longing to go home, pressed me in haste.

sentences.zh: 」因拜正言，厚加慰撫。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bowed to Zhengyan and greatly comforted and soothed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bowed to Zhengyan and comforted him warmly.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，正言求為平盧軍行軍司馬，因以授之，竟卒於任。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zhengyan requested to be campaigning marshal of the Pinglu army and was therefore granted it; in the end he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Zhengyan asked to be made campaigning marshal of the Pinglu army and was appointed; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 胡裝，禮部尚書曾之孫。

translations.literal: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, former minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 汴將楊師厚之鎮魏州，裝與副使李嗣業有舊，因往依之，薦授貴鄉令。

translations.literal: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was stationed at Weizhou, Zhuang had old ties with the deputy commissioner Li Siye and therefore went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was posted to Weizhou, Zhuang, who had old ties with deputy commissioner Li Siye, went to join him and was recommended for appointment as magistrate of Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 及張彥之亂，嗣業遇害，裝罷秩，客於魏州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yan's rebellion occurred, Siye met with harm; Zhuang lost his post and lodged as a guest in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan rebelled, Siye was killed. Zhuang lost his post and lived as a guest in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初至，裝謁見，求假官，司空頲以其居官貪濁，不得調者久之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional appointment. Sikong Hui, because he had been corrupt and foul in office, long would not allow his transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought an appointment. Sikong Hui, citing Zhuang's corrupt conduct in office, long refused to approve his transfer.

sentences.zh: 十三年，莊宗還太原，裝候於離亭；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan, Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;

sentences.zh: 謁者不內，乃排闥而入，曰：「臣本朝公卿子孫，從兵至此。

translations.literal: the usher would not admit him, so he pushed open the door and entered, saying, "Your subject is a descendant of this dynasty's high ministers; I have followed the army to this place.
translations.idiomatic: the usher would not admit him, so he forced his way in and said, "I am a descendant of this dynasty's high ministers and have followed the army here.

sentences.zh: 殿下比襲唐祚，勤求英俊，以壯霸圖。

translations.literal: Your Highness recently inherited the Tang succession and diligently sought outstanding men to strengthen the hegemonic design.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has lately taken up the Tang succession and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen your great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不才，比於進九九，納豎刁、頭須，亦所庶幾。

translations.literal: Though your subject lacks talent, compared with presenting the nine-nine, or taking in Shu Diao and Tou Xu, it is also what one might hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack talent, I am no worse than those who presented the nine-nine tortoise or brought in favorites like Shu Diao and Tou Xu.

sentences.zh: 而羈旅累年，執事者不垂顧錄，臣不能赴海觸樹，走胡適越，今日歸死於殿下也！

translations.literal: Yet for years in exile those in charge have not looked down to record me. Your subject cannot go to the sea and strike the tree, or flee to Hu and suit Yue—today I return to die before Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: Yet for years in exile those in charge have ignored me. I cannot throw myself into the sea or flee abroad—I come today to die before Your Highness!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗愕然曰：「孤未之知，何至如是！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I did not know of this—how could it reach such a point!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I knew nothing of this—how could it come to this!

sentences.zh: 」賜酒食慰遣之，謂郭崇韜曰：「便與擬議。

translations.literal: " He granted wine and food, comforted him, and sent him away, saying to Guo Chongtao, "At once draw up a proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him wine and food, comforted him, and sent him away, telling Guo Chongtao, "Draw up an appointment at once.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，署館驛巡官。

translations.literal: " That year he was assigned as touring officer of the post stations.
translations.idiomatic: " That year he was appointed touring officer of the post stations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授監察御史裏行，遷節度巡官，賜緋魚袋；

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed acting investigating censor, promoted to touring officer of the military commission, and granted scarlet robes and the fish tally;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting investigating censor, then promoted to touring officer of the military commission and granted scarlet robes and the fish tally;

sentences.zh: 尋曆推官、檢校員外郎。

translations.literal: shortly thereafter he successively served as pushi and acting director of a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: and soon served successively as pushi and acting director of a ministry.

sentences.zh: 裝學書無師法，工詩非作者，僻於題壁，所至宮亭寺觀，必書爵裏，人或譏之，不以為愧。

translations.literal: Zhuang studied calligraphy without master's method; he was skilled at poetry but not an author. He was eccentric in writing on walls—wherever he went, at palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he always wrote his rank and native place. People sometimes mocked him, but he did not feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper training and wrote verse without real literary merit. He had a habit of inscribing walls—at every palace, pavilion, temple, and shrine he visited he wrote his rank and birthplace. People mocked him, but he felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 時四鎮幕賓皆金紫，裝獨恥銀艾。

translations.literal: At that time staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and azure.
translations.idiomatic: Staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple insignia, but Zhuang alone was ashamed of his silver and azure.

sentences.zh: 十七年，莊宗自魏州之德勝，與賓僚城樓餞別，既而群僚離席，裝獨留，獻詩三篇，意在章服。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong went from Weizhou to Desheng and on the city tower took leave of his guests and staff. After the group of staff had left their seats, Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his intent being official robes and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong left Weizhou for Desheng and on the city tower bade farewell to his staff. When the others had left the table, Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, aiming to win higher robes and insignia.

sentences.zh: 莊宗舉大鍾屬裝曰：「員外能釂此乎？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and entrusted it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raised a great goblet and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?

sentences.zh: 」裝飲酒素少，略無難色，為之一舉而釂，莊宗即解紫袍賜之。

translations.literal: " Zhuang ordinarily drank little, but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one lift. Zhuangzong immediately removed his purple robe and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuang ordinarily drank little, but showed no hesitation and drained it in one draft. Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 同光初，以裝為給事中，從幸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant censor and followed on the journey of favor to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tongguang era he was made attendant censor and accompanied the emperor to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時連年大水，百官多窘，裝求為襄州副使。

translations.literal: At that time floods continued year after year and many officials were in straits; Zhuang requested to be deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Floods had afflicted the realm for years and many officials were impoverished. Zhuang asked to be made deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，洛陽變擾，節度使劉訓以私忿族裝，誣奏雲裝欲謀亂，人士冤之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Luoyang was disturbed by upheaval, the military commissioner Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended to plot rebellion. Men of standing held it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the turmoil in Luoyang, military commissioner Liu Xun, from private enmity, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely reported that Zhuang had plotted rebellion. Scholars and officials regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 崔貽孫，

translations.literal: Cui Yisun,
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yisun,

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·宰相世係表》：貽孫字伯垂。）〉

translations.literal: (Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages in the New Book of Tang: Yisun's courtesy name was Bochui.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages: Yisun's courtesy name was Bochui.)〉

sentences.zh: 祖元亮，左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanliang was left attendant cavalry regular.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanliang was left attendant cavalry regular.

sentences.zh: （《世係表》：元亮，字晦孫，虢州刺史。）〉

translations.literal: (Tables of Lineages: Yuanliang, courtesy name Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Tables of Lineages: Yuanliang, courtesy name Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉

sentences.zh: 父芻言，潞州判官。

translations.literal: His father Chuyan was judicial aide of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuyan was judicial aide of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以門族登進士第，以監察升朝，曆清資美職。

translations.literal: Yisun through his clan status passed the jinshi examination, rose to court through investigating censor, and successively held pure-capital and fine posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun passed the jinshi examination through his family's standing, entered court as investigating censor, and held a series of prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 及為省郎，使於江南回，以橐裝營別墅於漢上之穀城，退居自奉。

translations.literal: When he became a ministry secretary and returned from a mission to Jiangnan, he used his traveling funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a ministry secretary and returned from a mission to the south, he used his travel funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired there to live on his own means.

sentences.zh: 清江之上，綠竹遍野，狹徑濃密，維舟曲岸，人莫造焉，時人甚高之。

translations.literal: Above the clear river green bamboo spread over the fields; narrow paths were thick and dense; he moored his boat on the winding bank, and people did not venture there. Men of the time greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Green bamboo spread along the clear river, the paths were narrow and overgrown, and he moored his boat on a winding bank where no one disturbed him. Contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及李振貶均州，貽孫曲奉之。

translations.literal: When Li Zhen was demoted to Junzhou, Yisun attended him with bent service.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhen was demoted to Junzhou, Yisun attended him with elaborate deference.

sentences.zh: 振入朝，貽孫累遷丞郎。

translations.literal: When Zhen entered court, Yisun was repeatedly promoted to director and secretary posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen returned to court, Yisun rose repeatedly to director and secretary posts.

sentences.zh: 同光初，除吏部侍郎，銓選疏謬，貶官塞地，馳驛至潞州，致書於府帥孔曰：「十五年穀城山裏，自謂逸人；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed vice minister of personnel; his selection was careless and erroneous, and he was demoted to a frontier post. He galloped by post relay to Luzhou and sent a letter to the prefect Kong, saying, "For fifteen years in the Gucheng mountains I called myself a recluse;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tongguang era he was made vice minister of personnel, but his selections were careless and he was demoted to a frontier post. He rode post-haste to Luzhou and wrote to the prefect Kong: "For fifteen years in the Gucheng mountains I called myself a recluse;

sentences.zh: 二千里沙塞途中，今為逐客。

translations.literal: on the two-thousand-li road through desert and pass, today I am an expelled guest.
translations.idiomatic: on a two-thousand-li road through desert and frontier passes, I am now an exile.

sentences.zh: 」以其年八十，奏留府下。

translations.literal: " Because he was eighty years old, a memorial was submitted to keep him under the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Because he was eighty, a memorial was submitted to keep him at the prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 明年，量移澤州司馬，遇赦還京。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred by degree to military aide of Zezhou; he met an amnesty and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to military aide of Zezhou, then returned to the capital under an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭玨以姻戚之分，復擬吏部侍郎，天官任重，昏耄罔知，後遷禮部尚書，致仕而卒。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zheng Jue, because of ties of marriage kinship, again proposed him as vice minister of personnel. The Ministry of Heaven's office was weighty in responsibility, but he was senile and knew nothing; later he was moved to minister of rites, retired from office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zheng Jue, a kinsman by marriage, again proposed him as vice minister of personnel. The post was weighty, but Yisun was senile and incompetent. He was later made minister of rites, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：崔貽孫年過八十，求進不休，囊橐之資，素有貯積，性好幹人，喜得小惠。）〉

translations.literal: (Miscellaneous Words from Northern Dreams: Cui Yisun passed eighty years but did not cease seeking advancement; funds in purse and bag he had long stored up; by nature he liked to meddle with people and delighted in receiving small favors.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Miscellaneous Words from Northern Dreams: Cui Yisun was past eighty but never ceased seeking advancement. He had long hoarded his wealth, loved to meddle in others' affairs, and delighted in small favors.)〉

sentences.zh: 有子三人，自貽孫左降之後，各於舊業爭分其利，甘旨醫藥，莫有奉者。

translations.literal: He had three sons. After Yisun's demotion each contended for a share of the profits from his old enterprises; for fine food and medicine there was no one who attended him.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. After his demotion each fought over a share of his old property, and none provided him food or medicine.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以書責之云：「生有明君宰相，死有天曹地府，吾雖考終，豈放汝耶！」

translations.literal: Yisun wrote to reprove them, saying, "In life there are enlightened rulers and chief ministers; in death there are the heavenly bureau and the underworld. Though I may die a natural death, how could I release you!"
translations.idiomatic: Yisun wrote to reproach them: "In life there are enlightened rulers and chief ministers; in death there are heaven's court and the underworld. Though I may die a natural death, do you think I will let you go!"

sentences.zh: 孟鵠，魏州人。

translations.literal: Meng Hu was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hu was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初定魏博，選幹吏以計兵賦，以鵠為度支孔目官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo he selected capable officials to calculate troops and levies and made Hu a clerical officer of the revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo he chose capable officials to calculate troops and levies and appointed Hu a clerical officer of the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為邢洺節度使，每曲意承迎，明宗甚德之。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's time he was military commissioner of Xing and Mo; he always bent his intent to welcome and please, and Mingzong greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was military commissioner of Xing and Mo and always went out of his way to please him; Mingzong thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 及孔謙專典軍賦，徵督苛急，明宗嘗切齒。

translations.literal: When Kong Qian monopolized control of military levies and collection and exaction were harsh and urgent, Mingzong once ground his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Qian monopolized military levies and his collections were harsh and relentless, Mingzong once ground his teeth in anger.

sentences.zh: 及即位，鵠自租庸勾官擢為客省副使、樞密承旨，遷三司副使，出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Hu was promoted from grain-and-corvée checking officer to deputy commissioner of the guest bureau and bearer of edicts at the Bureau of Military Affairs, moved to deputy commissioner of the three bureaus, and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Hu was promoted from grain-and-corvée checking officer to deputy commissioner of the guest bureau and bearer of edicts at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then made deputy commissioner of the three bureaus and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會範延光再遷樞密，乃征鵠為三司使。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang was again moved to the Bureau of Military Affairs, Hu was summoned as commissioner of the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang was again appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs, Hu was summoned to be commissioner of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 初，鵠有計畫之能，及專掌邦賦，操割依違，名譽頓減。

translations.literal: At first Hu had the capacity for planning; when he monopolized control of state levies, his grasping and cutting were inconsistent, and his reputation suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hu had a talent for planning, but once he controlled state revenue his exactions were arbitrary and his reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 期年發疾，求外任，仍授許州節度使。

translations.literal: Within a year he fell ill, sought an outer appointment, and was still granted military commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he fell ill, sought a post outside the capital, and was made military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 謝恩退，帝目送之，顧為侍臣曰：「孟鵠掌三司幾年，得至方鎮？

translations.literal: After thanking the emperor for grace and withdrawing, the emperor watched him go with his eyes and turned to the attending ministers, saying, "Meng Hu managed the three bureaus for how many years to reach a frontier command?
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew after thanking the emperor, the emperor watched him go and said to his attendants, "How many years did Meng Hu run the three bureaus to reach a frontier command?

sentences.zh: 」範延光奏曰：「鵠於同光世已為三司勾官，天成初為三司副使，出刺相州，入判三司又二年。

translations.literal: " Fan Yanguang memorialized, saying, "Hu was already a checking officer of the three bureaus in the Tongguang era; at the beginning of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner of the three bureaus, went out as prefect of Xiang, and entered to judge the three bureaus for another two years.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Yanguang replied, "Hu was already a checking officer of the three bureaus in the Tongguang era. At the beginning of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner, then prefect of Xiang, and after returning to judge the three bureaus served another two years.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「鵠以幹事，遽至方鎮，爭不勉旃。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Hu, through handling affairs, swiftly reached a frontier command—how could one not urge him on!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Hu reached a frontier command so quickly through his competence—who would not urge him on!

sentences.zh: 」鵠與延光俱魏人，厚相結托，暨延光掌樞務，援引判三司，又致節鉞，明宗知之，故以此言譏之。

translations.literal: " Hu and Yanguang were both men of Wei and formed a thick mutual bond. When Yanguang took charge of military affairs he recommended Hu to judge the three bureaus and also secured for him a military commissioner's seal and axe. Mingzong knew this and therefore used these words to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu and Yanguang were both from Wei and were closely allied. When Yanguang took charge of military affairs he secured Hu's appointment to the three bureaus and then a military commission. Mingzong knew this and spoke with sarcasm.

sentences.zh: 到任未周歲，卒。

translations.literal: He had not completed a year in his post when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died less than a year after taking office.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 孫嶽，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yue was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yue was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 強幹有才用，曆府衛右職。

translations.literal: Strong and capable with talent and usefulness, he successively held right-hand posts in the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was forceful and capable and held a series of posts in the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為潁耀二州刺史、閬州團練使，所至稱治，遷鳳州節度使。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he was prefect of the two prefectures Ying and Yao and regimental trainer of Langzhou; wherever he went he was praised for good governance, and he was moved to military commissioner of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he served as prefect of Ying and Yao and as regimental trainer of Langzhou. Wherever he went he was praised for good governance, and he was promoted to military commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 受代歸京，秦王從榮欲以嶽為元帥府都押衙，事未行，馮贇舉為三司使，時預密謀。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived he returned to the capital. Prince of Qin Congrong wished to make Yue chief military adjutant of the marshal's headquarters; the matter had not been carried out when Feng Yun recommended him as commissioner of the three bureaus, at the time participating in secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to the capital. Prince of Qin Congrong wished to make Yue chief military adjutant of his headquarters, but before this could happen Feng Yun recommended him as commissioner of the three bureaus while he was involved in secret plotting.

sentences.zh: 朱、馮患從榮之恣橫，嶽曾極言其禍之端，康義誠聞之不悅。

translations.literal: Zhu and Feng were troubled by Congrong's wanton arrogance; Yue had once spoken to the utmost about the beginnings of his calamity. Kang Yicheng heard of it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Feng were troubled by Congrong's arrogance. Yue had once spoken at length about the danger he posed. Kang Yicheng heard of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及從榮敗，義誠召嶽同至河南府檢閱府藏。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, Yicheng summoned Yue to go together to the Henan prefectural office to inspect the prefectural stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong was defeated, Yicheng summoned Yue to join him at the Henan prefectural office to inspect the treasury.

sentences.zh: 時紛擾未定，義誠密遣騎士射之，嶽走至通利坊，為騎士所害，識與不識皆痛之。

translations.literal: At that time turmoil was not yet settled; Yicheng secretly sent horsemen to shoot him. Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was harmed by the horsemen. Those who knew him and those who did not alike grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil had not yet subsided. Yicheng secretly sent horsemen to shoot him. Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed. All who knew him, and many who did not, grieved.

sentences.zh: 子璉，曆諸衛將軍、藩閫節度副使。

translations.literal: His son Lian successively held the posts of general of the guards and deputy military commissioner of a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian served successively as a guard general and as deputy military commissioner of a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 張延朗，汴州開封人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang was a man of Kaifeng in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang was a native of Kaifeng in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 事梁，以租庸吏為鄆州糧料使。

translations.literal: He served Liang and, as a grain-and-corvée clerk, was made grain supply commissioner of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liang as a grain-and-corvée clerk and was made grain supply commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗克鄆州，得延朗，復以為糧料使，後徙鎮宣武、成德，以為元從孔目官。

translations.literal: When Mingzong captured Yanzhou he obtained Yanlang and again made him grain supply commissioner; later, when he moved his command to Xuanwu and Chengde, he made him a clerical officer among his original followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong captured Yanzhou he took Yanlang into service and again made him grain supply commissioner. Later, when Mingzong moved his command to Xuanwu and Chengde, he made Yanlang a clerical officer among his original followers.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，始置三司使，拜延朗特進、工部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，兼判戶部度支事，詔以延朗充三司使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing the post of commissioner of the three bureaus was first established; Yanlang was appointed specially advanced and minister of works, made commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits and concurrently judge of revenue affairs in the Ministry of Revenue, and by edict made commissioner of the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1 the post of commissioner of the three bureaus was first established. Yanlang was appointed specially advanced and minister of works, made commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits and concurrently placed in charge of revenue affairs in the Ministry of Revenue, and by edict made commissioner of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，授禮部尚書，兼中書侍郎、平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was granted minister of rites, concurrently vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief minister, and judge of the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Yanlang was made minister of rites, concurrently vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief minister, and commissioner of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 延朗再上表辭曰：

translations.literal: Yanlang again submitted a memorial declining, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang again submitted a memorial of refusal, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣濫承雨露，擢處鈞衡，兼叨選部之銜，仍掌計司之重。

translations.literal: Your subject has rashly received the rain and dew, been promoted to the balance beam, and concurrently bears the title of the selection ministry while still holding the weight of the accounting bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has undeservedly received imperial favor, been raised to the chief ministership, and at the same time holds a post in the selection ministry while still bearing the weight of the revenue office.

sentences.zh: 況中省文章之地，洪爐陶鑄之門，臣自揣量，何以當處。

translations.literal: Moreover the central secretariat is the place of literary composition, the great furnace and casting gate; your subject measures himself—how could he fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: The central secretariat is the seat of state writing and the great forge of talent. When I measure myself, how can I be fit for such a post?

sentences.zh: 是以繼陳章表，疊貢情誠，乞請睿恩，免貽朝論。

translations.literal: Therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials and piled up offerings of sincere feeling, begging imperial grace to spare me from bringing reproach on court discussion.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore submitted memorial after memorial, earnestly begging your grace to spare me from bringing reproach upon the court.

sentences.zh: 豈謂禦批累降，聖旨不移，決以此官，委臣非器，所以強收涕泗，勉遏怔忪，重思事上之門，細料盡忠之路。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that imperial rescripts would descend repeatedly and the sacred intent would not shift, firmly committing this office to your subject though he is no fit vessel! Therefore I forcibly restrain tears, strive to check my bewilderment, think again on the gate of serving the sovereign, and carefully reckon the path of utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet imperial rescripts have come again and again and your sacred intent has not changed—you have firmly entrusted this office to one unfit for it. I therefore force back my tears, steady my confusion, and think again on how to serve my sovereign and fulfill my duty.

sentences.zh: 竊以位高則危至，寵極則謗生，君臣莫保於初終，分義難防於毀譽。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that when position is high, peril arrives; when favor reaches its peak, slander is born. Lord and minister cannot be preserved from beginning to end; allotted duty is hard to guard against ruin and praise.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to believe that high position brings danger, and extreme favor breeds slander. Lord and minister seldom keep faith from beginning to end, and duty is hard to defend against praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 臣若保茲重任，忘彼至公，徇情而以免是非，偷安而以固富貴，則內欺心腑，外負聖朝，何以報君父之大恩，望子孫之延慶。

translations.literal: If your subject preserves this weighty responsibility yet forgets that utmost public-mindedness, follows private feeling to escape right and wrong, or seeks ease to secure wealth and honor, then inwardly he deceives his heart and outwardly he fails the sacred court—how could he repay the great grace of sovereign and father or hope for extended blessing for his descendants?
translations.idiomatic: If I hold this weighty post yet forget the public good, follow private feeling to escape blame, or seek ease to secure wealth and rank, I would deceive my own heart and fail the court. How could I repay your great grace or hope for blessing on my descendants?

sentences.zh: 臣若但行王道，惟守國章，任人必取當才，決事須依正理，確違形勢，堅塞幸門，則可以振舉宏綱，彌縫大化，助陛下含容之澤，彰國家至理之風，然而讒邪者必起憾詞，憎嫉者寧無謗議，或慮至尊未悉，群謗難明，不更拔本尋源，便俟甘瑕受玷，臣心可忍，臣恥可消。

translations.literal: If your subject only practices the kingly way, solely guards the state's statutes, in employing men must take the fitting talent, and in deciding affairs must rely on correct principle, firmly opposing trends and solidly blocking the gate of favor, then he can raise up the great framework and mend the great transformation, assist Your Majesty's tolerant grace and display the state's utmost rational wind. Yet slanderers and the wicked will surely raise words of resentment; those who hate and envy will rather not be without words of calumny. Perhaps one fears the supreme lord has not yet understood and the crowd of slanders is hard to clarify—not to pull up the root and seek the source, but to await willingly accepting stain upon flaw: your subject's heart could bear it, but your subject's shame could not be erased.
translations.idiomatic: If I practice the kingly way alone, uphold the laws of the state, appoint only the fit, and decide all matters by right principle, firmly resisting trends and closing the door to favor, I may strengthen the great order and help your tolerant rule display the nation's highest principles. Yet slanderers will raise complaints and the envious will not lack for calumny. I fear your Majesty may not see the truth, and if I do not strike at the root but willingly accept stain upon stain, my heart could bear it—but my shame could not be erased.

sentences.zh: 隻恐山林草澤之人，稱量聖製；

translations.literal: I only fear that men of mountains, forests, marshes, and meadows will measure the sacred system;
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that recluses in mountains and marshes will weigh your sacred rule;

sentences.zh: 冠履軒裳之士，輕慢朝廷。

translations.literal: and gentlemen of caps, shoes, carriages, and robes will lightly treat the court with disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: and gentlemen in caps and robes will look down on the court.

sentences.zh: 臣又以國計一司，掌其經費，利權二務，職在捃收。

translations.literal: Your subject further considers that the state accounts are one bureau controlling its expenditures; profit and authority are two duties whose office lies in gathering and collecting.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject further notes that state accounts are managed by one bureau controlling expenditures, while profit and authority are two duties whose task is collection.

sentences.zh: 將欲養四海之貧民，無過薄賦；

translations.literal: If one wishes to nourish the poor people of the four seas, nothing surpasses light levies;
translations.idiomatic: To support the poor throughout the realm, nothing surpasses light taxation;

sentences.zh: 贍六軍之勁士，又藉豐儲。

translations.literal: to supply the stalwart warriors of the six armies, one again relies on abundant stores.
translations.idiomatic: to supply the stalwart warriors of the six armies, one must also rely on full storehouses.

sentences.zh: 利害相隨，取與難酌，若使罄山采木，竭澤求魚，則地官之教化不行，國本之傷殘益甚，取怨黔首，是黷皇風。

translations.literal: Benefit and harm follow each other; taking and giving are hard to measure. If one makes the mountains empty in gathering wood and drains the marshes to seek fish, then the Minister of Earth's instruction will not be carried out, the state's foundation will be injured and crippled all the more, one will draw the resentment of the black-haired people, and this is to profane the imperial wind.
translations.idiomatic: Benefit and harm go together, and what to take and what to give are hard to balance. If we strip the mountains for timber and drain the marshes for fish, the Minister of Earth's teaching will not prevail, the foundation of the state will be further harmed, the people will resent us, and we will profane the imperial way.

sentences.zh: 況諸道所征賦租，雖多數額，時逢水旱，或遇蟲霜，其間則有減無添，所在又申逃係欠。

translations.literal: Moreover the levies and rents collected by the various circuits, though numerous in quota, at times meet flood and drought or encounter insects and frost; among them there is decrease but no increase, and everywhere they also report flight, attachment, and arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the levies collected by the circuits are large in quota, floods, drought, insects, and frost often reduce them. Decreases are common and increases rare, and everywhere officials report flight, attachment, and arrears.

sentences.zh: 乃至軍儲官俸，常汲汲於供須；

translations.literal: As for military stores and official salaries, they are constantly urgent in supply;
translations.idiomatic: Military stores and official salaries are constantly urgent in their demands;

sentences.zh: 夏稅秋租，每懸懸於繼續。

translations.literal: summer tax and autumn rent are each suspended in continuing succession.
translations.idiomatic: summer tax and autumn rent hang perpetually in arrears.

sentences.zh: 況今內外倉庫，多是罄空；

translations.literal: Moreover at present inner and outer storehouses are mostly emptied;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, inner and outer storehouses are now mostly empty;

sentences.zh: 遠近生民，或聞饑歉。

translations.literal: near and far the living people sometimes hear of famine and dearth.
translations.idiomatic: and among the people near and far there are reports of famine.

sentences.zh: 伏惟朝廷尚添軍額，更益師徒，非時之博糴難為，異日之區分轉大。

translations.literal: I bow that the court still adds military quotas and further increases troops and masters; untimely broad purchase of grain is hard to accomplish, and the division of categories on another day will turn greater.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that the court is still adding military quotas and increasing troops. Emergency grain purchases are hard to sustain, and the burden will only grow greater in time.

sentences.zh: 竊慮年支有闕，國計可憂。

translations.literal: I venture to fear that annual expenditure will have gaps and state accounts may be worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: I fear annual expenditure will fall short and the state accounts will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 望陛下節例外之破除，放諸項以儉省，不添冗食，且止新兵，務急去繁，以寬經費，減奢從儉，漸俟豐盈，則屈者知恩，叛者從化，弭兵有日，富俗可期。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will restrain extraordinary removals, release various items for frugal saving, not add redundant eaters, and for the time being halt new troops; urgently seek to remove complexity to broaden expenditures, reduce extravagance and follow economy, gradually await abundance and fullness—then the bent will know grace, rebels will follow transformation, arms may be stilled within days, and a rich custom may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will cut extraordinary spending, release various levies for economy, add no redundant offices, halt new recruitment, urgently reduce complexity to ease expenditures, practice frugality, and gradually await abundance. Then the oppressed will know grace, rebels will submit, arms may be laid down, and prosperity may be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞治民尚清，為政務易，易則煩苛並去，清則偏黨無施。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that in governing the people clarity is esteemed and in conducting government ease is the task; when there is ease, vexation and severity are both removed; when there is clarity, partial factions are not applied.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that in governing the people clarity is prized and in conducting government simplicity is essential. With simplicity, harsh regulations are removed; with clarity, partisan favoritism ceases.

sentences.zh: 若擇其良牧，委在正人，則境內蒸黎，必獲蘇息，官中倉庫，亦絕侵欺。

translations.literal: If one selects good shepherds and entrusts them to upright men, then the common people within the borders will surely obtain relief and revival, and official storehouses will also cut off invasion and fraud.
translations.idiomatic: If good governors are chosen and upright men entrusted with office, the people within the borders will surely recover, and official storehouses will be free of embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 伏望誡見在之處官，無乖撫俗；

translations.literal: I bow in hope to admonish the officials now in place not to depart from soothing the customs;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope Your Majesty will admonish officials now in office not to fail in comforting the people;

sentences.zh: 擇將來之蒞事，更審求賢。

translations.literal: in selecting those who will come to hold affairs, further carefully seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: and in choosing those who will hold office hereafter, seek the worthy with greater care.

sentences.zh: 儻一一得人，則農無所苦；

translations.literal: If in each case one obtains the right man, then farmers will have no suffering;
translations.idiomatic: If the right man is found in every case, farmers will suffer no hardship;

sentences.zh: 人人致理，則國復何憂。

translations.literal: if every man brings order, then what worry has the state?
translations.idiomatic: if every man brings order to his charge, what worry remains for the state?

sentences.zh: 但奉公善政者，不惜重酬；

translations.literal: Only those who serve the public with good government—do not spare heavy reward;
translations.idiomatic: Only let those who serve the public with good government receive generous reward;

sentences.zh: 昧理無功者，勿頒厚俸。

translations.literal: Those who are dark to principle and without achievement—do not bestow thick salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are ignorant of principle and achieve nothing should not receive generous salaries.

sentences.zh: 益彰有道，兼絕徇情。

translations.literal: This further displays the way and at the same time cuts off following private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: This will further display the right way and at the same time cut off favoritism.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下，念臣布露之前言，閔臣驚憂於後患，察臣愚直，杜彼讒邪，臣即但副天心，不防人口，庶幾萬一，仰答聖明。

translations.literal: I bow in hope that Your Majesty will recall your subject's earlier words laid bare, pity your subject's alarm and worry over later calamity, perceive your subject's dull uprightness, block those slanderers and the wicked—your subject will then only accord with Heaven's heart and not guard against people's mouths, hoping in the one in ten thousand to look up and answer sacred clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope Your Majesty will recall my earlier frank words, pity my alarm over future troubles, perceive my dull integrity, and block slanderers and the wicked. I will then follow Heaven's intent alone and not fear men's tongues, hoping in the smallest measure to answer your sacred clarity.

sentences.zh: 末帝優詔答之，召於便殿，謂之曰：「卿所論奏，深中時病，形之切言，頗救朕失。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor answered with a gracious edict, summoned him to the informal hall, and said to him, "What you have discussed and memorialized deeply hits the illness of the times; formed in cutting words, it considerably rescues Our faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor replied with a gracious edict and summoned him to the informal hall, saying, "Your memorial strikes deep at the ills of the times. Your forthright words have done much to correct Our errors.

sentences.zh: 國計事重，日得商量，無勞過慮也。

translations.literal: State accounts are weighty affairs; we may consult day by day—no need for excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: State revenue is a weighty matter. We can consult on it daily—do not trouble yourself with excessive worry.

sentences.zh: 」延朗不得已而承命。

translations.literal: " Yanlang had no alternative but to accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanlang had no choice but to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 延朗有心計，善理繁劇。

translations.literal: Yanlang had schemes in his heart and was skilled at managing complexity and urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang was shrewd and skilled at managing complex and urgent affairs.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖在太原，朝廷猜忌，不欲令有積聚，係官財貨留使之外，延朗悉遣取之，晉高祖深銜其事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to have accumulations. Beyond the official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all, and Gaozu of Jin deeply harbored resentment over this affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate wealth. Beyond the official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to seize them all, and Gaozu deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 及晉陽起兵，末帝議親征，然亦采浮論，不能果決；

translations.literal: When troops were raised at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated on a personal campaign, yet he also adopted floating opinions and could not reach a firm decision;
translations.idiomatic: When troops were raised at Jinyang the Last Emperor considered leading a campaign in person, but he also heeded shallow counsel and could not decide firmly;

sentences.zh: 延朗獨排眾議，請末帝北行，識者韙之。

translations.literal: Yanlang alone rejected the crowd's opinions and requested that the Last Emperor march north; men of insight approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang alone rejected the majority view and urged the Last Emperor to march north, and men of insight approved.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入洛，送台獄以誅之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent him to the metropolitan prison and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent Yanlang to the metropolitan prison and executed him.

sentences.zh: 其後以選求計使，難得其人，甚追悔焉。

translations.literal: Afterward, in selecting and seeking a revenue commissioner, it was hard to obtain the right man, and he deeply regretted it.
