translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when seeking a commissioner of revenue, no suitable man could be found, and the court deeply regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 劉延朗，宋州虞城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang was a man of Yucheng in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang was a native of Yucheng in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 末帝鎮河中時，為鄆城馬步都虞候，後納為腹心。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was stationed at Hezhong he was chief military inspector of horse and foot at Yancheng; later he was taken in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor was posted to Hezhong, Yanlang was chief military inspector of horse and foot at Yancheng and was later taken into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 及鎮鳳翔，署為孔目吏。

translations.literal: When he was stationed at Fengxiang he was assigned as a clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor was posted to Fengxiang, he appointed Yanlang a clerical officer.

sentences.zh: 末帝將圖起義，為捍禦之備，延朗計公私粟帛，以贍其急。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was about to plan an uprising and make preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply their urgency.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor planned his uprising and prepared for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to meet their urgent needs.

sentences.zh: 及西師納降，末帝赴洛，皆無所闕焉，末帝甚賞之。

translations.literal: When the western army submitted and surrendered and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking; the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was wanting, and the Last Emperor greatly commended him.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，除宣徽北院使，俄以劉延皓守鄴，改副樞密使，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat; shortly thereafter, because Liu Yanhao guarded Ye, he was changed to deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and successively reached acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat. Soon afterward, when Liu Yanhao was posted to guard Ye, he was made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and eventually rose to acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 時房皓為樞密使，但高枕閑眠，啟奏除授，一歸延朗，由是得志。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs but only rested his head high and slept at leisure; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and by this he got his will.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs but slept at ease and left all memorials for appointments and dismissals to Yanlang, who thereby had his way.

sentences.zh: 凡藩侯郡牧，自外入者，必先賂延朗，後議進貢，賂厚者先居內地，賂薄者晚出邊藩，故諸將屢有怨訕，末帝不能察之。

translations.literal: Whenever feudal lords and prefectural governors came in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and afterward discuss tribute. Those who bribed thickly were first placed in inner territories; those who bribed thinly were late in going out to frontier commands. Therefore the various generals repeatedly had resentment and ridicule, but the Last Emperor could not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever frontier lords and prefects came to court from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang before their tribute was discussed. Those who bribed heavily were posted first to inner territories; those who bribed lightly were sent late to frontier commands. The generals often complained, but the Last Emperor did not perceive it.

sentences.zh: 及晉高祖入洛，延朗將竄於南山，與從者數輩，過其私第，指而歎曰：「我有錢三十萬貫聚於此，不知為何人所得。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee to the southern mountains. With several followers he passed his private residence, pointed, and sighed, saying, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know into whose hands it will fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee to the southern mountains. With several followers he passed his private residence, pointed at it, and sighed: "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash hoarded here—I do not know who will get it.

sentences.zh: 」其愚暗如此。

translations.literal: " His stupidity and darkness were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: " His folly was such as this.

sentences.zh: 尋捕而殺之。

translations.literal: Shortly he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon captured and killed.
